newsitem.title: UK: NatWest hits record after "buy" ratings.
newsitem.headline: NatWest hits record after "buy" ratings.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc hit a record high on Wednesday amid continued demand following recent analyst recommendations on the stock, traders said.
NatWest shares were up 8-1/2p at 795 by 0850 GMT, after earlier rising as high as 797p -- surpassing the previous record of 795-1/2p set on January 21.

Dealers said the stock continued to gain strength from yesterday's "buy" recommendation from analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. "It is just a continuation of gains we saw yesterday," said one market-maker.

Another senior trader said, "There were some big buyers around yesterday, there is no stock around and the bank sector is still only going up." due to join the market later this year, dealers said fund managers were continuing to buy bank stocks to anticipate the sector's increased weighting within the FTSE 100 index.
"They have all got to get their weightings up," the senior trader said.
Analyst Peter Toeman at Hoare Govett pointed out that NatWest might have come back into favour after underperforming other leading bank stocks in recent months.

NatWest shares have risen sharply in the past month amid talk of a share buyback alongside forthcoming results and as analysts at brokerages including Panmure Gordon and Credit Lyonnais Laing issued "buy" recommendations.
NatWest is due to report 1996 earnings on February 25.
